title: forallx: An Introduction to Formal Logic — Chapters 23–29 (FOL language and syntax)
source: User-provided forallx Intro to Formal Logic PDF; PHIL 120 Unit 5

cards.prompt: In FOL, what does a name (like a or b) do?
options: Picks out exactly one object in the domain
Picks out a group of objects
Ranges over every object in the domain
cards.answer: A name picks out exactly one object in the domain.
cards.elaboration: Variables range over the domain; a name is fixed to one thing, like a proper noun.

cards.prompt: What is the domain in an FOL symbolization key?
options: The collection of things the quantifiers talk about
The names that appear in the argument
cards.answer: The domain is the collection of things the quantifiers range over.
cards.elaboration: With domain = people, ∀x H(x) says every person is happy, not every object.

cards.prompt: "Every alligator is a reptile." (A(x): x is an alligator, R(x): x is a reptile)
cards.elaboration: ∀x(A(x) ∧ R(x)) would say everything in the domain is an alligator.

cards.prompt: "Some reptile lives at the zoo." (R(x): reptile, Z(x): lives at the zoo)
cards.elaboration: ∃x(R(x) → Z(x)) is true as soon as anything is not a reptile, so it says almost nothing.

cards.prompt: "No spy knows the combination." (S(x): spy, K(x): knows the combination)
cards.elaboration: "No F is G" = every F is not G = there is no F that is G.

cards.prompt: "Only students are in the library." (S(x): student, L(x): in the library)
cards.answer: ∀x(L(x) → S(x)): anyone in the library is a student.
cards.elaboration: "Only F are G" flips the arrow compared with "all F are G".

cards.prompt: "Everyone loves someone." (domain: people, L(x,y): x loves y)
cards.answer: ∀x∃y L(x,y): each person has someone (maybe different) they love.
cards.elaboration: Order matters: ∃y∀x L(x,y) says one single person is loved by everyone.

cards.prompt: "There is someone whom everyone loves." (L(x,y): x loves y)
cards.answer: ∃y∀x L(x,y): one y such that every x loves y.
cards.elaboration: ∃x∀y L(x,y) is the reverse: someone who loves everyone.

cards.prompt: With L(x,y): x loves y, what does L(b,a) say?
options: a and b love each other
cards.answer: b loves a: the first slot is the lover, the second the loved.
cards.elaboration: Argument order in a many-place predicate follows the variable order in the key.

cards.prompt: "There are at least two apples." (A(x): x is an apple)
cards.elaboration: Without ¬x = y, x and y could be the same apple, so it would only say there is at least one.

cards.prompt: "There is exactly one apple." (A(x): x is an apple)
cards.answer: ∃x(A(x) ∧ ∀y(A(y) → x = y)): at least one, and any apple is that one.
cards.elaboration: ∀x∀y((A(x) ∧ A(y)) → x = y) alone means "at most one", true even with no apples.

cards.prompt: "Pavel owes money to everyone except Hikaru." (O(x,y): x owes money to y; names p, h)
cards.answer: ∀x(¬x = h → O(p,x)): everyone who isn't Hikaru is owed.
cards.elaboration: Identity lets FOL say "other than"; ∀x O(p,x) ∧ ¬O(p,h) contradicts itself.

cards.prompt: When is an FOL formula a sentence?
options: When it has no free variables
When it has at least one quantifier
cards.answer: A sentence is a formula with no free variables.
cards.elaboration: F(x) is a formula but not a sentence; ∃x F(x) and F(a) are sentences.

cards.prompt: In ∀x F(x) → G(x), is the x in G(x) bound?
options: No, it is free: ∀x only scopes over F(x)
Yes, ∀x binds every x after it
Yes, because the main connective is ∀
cards.answer: Free. Without brackets ∀x only scopes over F(x), and the main connective is →.
cards.elaboration: To bind both, write ∀x(F(x) → G(x)). So ∀x F(x) → G(x) is not a sentence.

cards.prompt: Russell's analysis of "The F is G" in FOL:
cards.answer: Exactly one thing is F, and it is G: ∃x(F(x) ∧ ∀y(F(y) → x = y) ∧ G(x)).
cards.elaboration: So "The present king of France is bald" comes out false, not meaningless: there is no such king.

cards.prompt: Why does "Every student read a book" need two FOL symbolizations?
options: It's ambiguous: one book for all, or maybe a different book each
Because books are not in the domain
cards.elaboration: Symbolizing forces a quantifier order, which picks one reading.
